## Introduction

### Overview

This session introduces basics of [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) - its three components
YAML (YAML Ain't Markup Language) header, code chunks and text. 
We will talk about the advantages of using Quarto. We will also learn to create
Quarto document, use several options to display/hide codes and 
figures and render Quarto document to html document. 

### Learning goals

In this session, you will learn:

- Basics of Quarto (syntax and formats)
- How to create and render a Quarto document in RStudio
- Components of Quarto such as YAML header, code chunks and text

Quarto is the next-generation version of R Markdown that allows to
combine prose, code, results. Quarto is not limited to single
programming language but is available in R, Python, Julia and
Observable. Here, we will focus to use Quarto in RStudio.

Quarto documents are reproducible and support different output formats
such as PDFs, Word files, presentations. It is a next generation R
Markdown that is built on Pandoc.

**Advantages of using Quarto:**

1.  Communicate with your collaborator: It includes code, results and
    steps
2.  Supports multi-format outputs such as HTML, PDF, Markdown, websites
    and more
3.  Reproducibility of research

**Note: Quarto is a command-line interface tool but not R package. Therefore, you do not need to install it separately. Rstudio has integrated Quarto to work with R.**

### Open a new Quarto document in Rstudio

Quarto file is a plain text file with `.qmd` extension. To create a new
Quarto document: File \> New File \> Quarto Document
![](../img/quarto_file_open.png){width="100%" fig-align="center"} This
will open a new window with several options. We can select the Quarto
outputs such as Documents, Presentation, interactive in different
formats. For example, for documents, we can pick HTML, PDF or Word
format. We can even choose Engine Knitr or Jupyter.

![](../img/new_quarto_doc.png){width="60%" fig-align="center"} This will
create an new unamed `Untitled.qmd` file. Lets rename it, by going to
`File`, `Save As` and `name of the file`

## Render a Quarto document

Rendering a Quarto document converts the .qmd document to the
requested format (html/pdf or any other frmat). During rendering, Quarto document(.qmd) 
is first processed using the knitr and then converted to the final format using pandoc. 
While rendering, all the code chunks are executed and the output is
embedded in the final document with the text. However, if there are 
any codes that produces error, your document will not be rendered.
To render a Quarto document, click on the `Render` button.
![](../img/render.png){width="80%" fig-align="center"}

### Components of Quarto:
1.  The YAML header surrounded by (`---`)
2.  Code chunk surrounded by (\`\`\`{r})
3.  Text- explanation of results

## YAML header

The header for the Quarto document is written in YAML language. It
allows to specify themes, formats, executable options and many more. Additionally,
it consists of series of metadata such as title, author date etc. 
You can think of YAML header as the settings of the Quarto document on how to process
and present your document. It is surrounded by (`---`), at the top of the Quarto document.
A simple example of YAML header is shown below:
![](../img/yaml_header.png){width="80%" fig-align="center"}
We can add some additional contents to the YAML header such as authors, date, theme
![](../img/yaml_header_1.png){width="40%" fig-align="center"}

Some of the additional contents of the YAML header can be found
[here](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-basics.html)

## Code chunks

Code chunks is a section where you can write the code and execute it. It
is enclosed in a three back ticks followed by `r`. You can write multiple
line of codes inside the code chunks.

Code chunks can be added in three different ways in RStudio:

1.  Keyboard commands: `Ctrl-Alt-I` (Windows) or `Cmd-Option-I` (Mac)
2.  Typing it manually - ```{r} and end it with ```
3.  Clicking the insert button
    ![](../img/insert_code_chunk.png){width="50%" fig-align="center"}


- You can include the comment inside the code chunk using the `#` symbol.
- Triangle sign with a line below execute all the code chunks before the current chunk.
- Triangle sign facing towards right/play button runs the current chunk.

## Chunk options

Several options can be added to the header of code chunk to customize the output of code. 
For instance,`echo: false` to hide the code, `message: false` to hide the messages or warnings, `fig-show=hide` to hide the figures
and many more. More options can be found [here] (https://quarto.org/docs/computations/execution-options.html).
Chunk options can be either written directly inside the curly braces 
(similar to the R Markdown) or by using #|(YAML syntax) before the code chunk where each #| line sets one option.

```{r echo=TRUE}
# Example code chunk
2*2
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
2*3
```

## Chunk labels 
Labeled code chunks can be useful due to several reasons:
1. It helps to refer the chunk in other places such as cross-referencing.
2. You can set up a network of certain chunks not to rerun to avoid the computational time.

```{r}
#| label: my-first-chunk
2 + 3
```

```{r}
#| label: my-second-chunk
5 * 6
```


## Run the code chunk:
1.  Click the green play button
2.  Keyboard shortcut: `Ctrl-Shift-Enter` (Windows) or `Cmd-Shift-Enter`
    (Mac)
3.  Place the cursor inside the chunk and press `Ctrl-Enter` (Windows)
    or `Cmd-Enter` (Mac)

Visualize output: You can visualize output either in the separate window or viewer pan. Type gear icon next to the Render would help to change the setting.

To produce the output, 1. click on the Render button at the top of the
script editor. 2. Press `Ctrl-Shift-K` (Windows) or `Cmd-Shift-K` (Mac)
to render the document. 3. Use command
quarto::quarto_render("filename.qmd") in the console.

**Inline code- The R code can be directly added in the text using single back ticks followed by `r` such as `r 2+2` which will produce `r 2+2` in the output document.**


## Global option
You can change the default option of the chunk.
Suppose you want to show just the figures and table without showing the command that 
produces it. You can do it in the Quarto YAML header under execute, by adding the following 
global option:`execute: echo :false`.
